pages.title: 300 Shorts Titles That Get Clicks: 2026 Edition
pages.body: 300 ready-to-use title templates in 10 categories. Replace the bracketed details with claims your video can prove.

pages.title: Before You Start: How to Use This Book
pages.body:
A strong title is a promise; your video must deliver on it. Create curiosity to earn clicks, but never promise results your video doesn't provide.

The 300 titles in this book are ready-to-copy phrases. Replace the bracketed sections with your own topic to use them as templates. Even if a title is bold, if your opening scene and conclusion don't fulfill its promise, you'll lose both viewer retention and trust.

How to use:
Replace [audience], [problem], [result], and [number] with details from your actual video. Make sure your title matches your opening caption and conclusion.

Avoid:
Don't use fake numbers, impossible results, unrelated people or events, or excessive fear/sexual innuendo to trick viewers into clicking.

Official guidelines:
https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/57404?hl=en - Titles: up to 100 characters
https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2801973?hl=en - Misleading metadata prohibited

A strong title quickly shows who, why, and what someone gains, while leaving one key question unanswered.

pages.title: The Title Formula
pages.body:
Build your title from five elements:

Audience: Who is this for? [Beginners]

Conflict: What problem, difference, or choice? [Mistake/Comparison]

Specifics: Numbers, timeframes, tools, or situations [3 items, 7 days]

Gap: What blank does the viewer want to fill in? [Reason/Result]

Reward: What value will viewers get? [Save money/Change]

You don't need all five. Choose two or three that fit your video best.

pages.title: Workshop: Picking the Right Title
pages.body:
Good titles aren't just flashes of inspiration—they come from options. Write 10 possible titles for your video, then narrow it down to the 3 that make the clearest promise. Compare those, and pick the 1 that matches your opening scene.

10 ideas: Mix different types to create candidates.

3 finalists: Compare audience, result, and curiosity.

1 test: Make sure your opening scene delivers on the promise.

Always answer the question your title creates before the end of your video.

pages.title: Bracket Replacement Guide
pages.body:
Just swap the bracketed text to use these templates instantly.

[audience]
Beginners, office workers, small business owners, creators

[topic]
Shorts, fitness, cooking, gaming, personal finance

[problem]
Lack of time, low views, repeated mistakes

[result]
Time saved, completion, growth, change

[action]
Edit, save, compare, buy, practice

[tool]
App, feature, template, equipment

[number]
3, 5, 7—use actual, provable numbers

[period]
10 minutes, 7 days, one month—use real timeframes

[A]/[B]
Free/paid, before/after, beginner/expert

[situation]
After work, before uploading, right after failure

3-second check after replacing:
- Is this actually in the video?
- Can viewers identify the audience in the opening scene?
- Does the conclusion answer the title's promise?
